## A pilot water-supply dashboard for the West Boundary

This site is a **pilot dashboard** supporting agricultural water supply and
storage planning in the **RDKB West Boundary** — the Kettle River watershed from
Midway upstream (Electoral Area E), including the communities of Baldy,
Beaverdell, Bridesville, Midway, and Rock Creek.

It brings public water information together in one accessible place to help
producers, First Nations, local government, and agencies share a common picture
of seasonal water conditions and drought risk. It is intended for **planning and
engagement only — not for regulatory monitoring**.

---

## Open the dashboard

**[→ West Boundary Water Security dashboard](water-security.qmd)**

The dashboard includes:

- **Current conditions** — live flow status for each monitoring station, scored
  against decades of record, with a project-area map of stations and communities.
- **Seasonal & drought risk** — this year's streamflow compared to the historical
  normal range, monthly climatology, and per-site comparisons.
- **Groundwater & aquifers** — water-table levels at Kettle valley observation
  wells (Grand Forks, Beaverdell, Midway) versus their historical norms.
- **Stations & live data** — the underlying monitoring network and live records.

---

## How it works

The dashboard combines **live readings** with **decades of historical record** to
show whether the watershed is tracking wetter or drier than normal for the time of
year. All information is **public and openly licensed**, and the whole tool is
built with open-source software so it can be fully owned and maintained by the
Regional District. See the **About** page for data sources and responsible-use
notes.
